decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “The draft covers … tags”; round 1 client: “saving links, tagging them … That's the shape I want.”
decisions.note: Specification-gate decision to support bookmark tagging conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only “search/filtering”; the client approves “searching and filtering.” Later rounds repeat those generic labels without defining tag-filter behavior or searchable fields.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the record does not establish whether filtering means selecting a specific tag or whether full-text search covers title, description, note, and URL. Generic approval does not resolve those details.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says the draft covers “editing”; rounds 4–5 continue with “Edit and delete” and “editing and deleting,” but no presentation specifies editing URL, title, description, tags, and note.
decisions.note: The editing decision remains underspecified through implementation review, so divergence from the required editable-field set cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “The draft covers … deletion”; round 1 client approves “deleting,” and later reviews continue to identify deletion as included.
decisions.note: The specification records bookmark deletion, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “duplicate detection”; round 4 describes the MVP as able to “catch duplicates.” Clients approve those descriptions, but no entry states that re-saving opens or guides editing of the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: Across specification and task review, duplicate detection is recorded but its disposition behavior remains unclear; approval does not establish reference-conforming edit-existing guidance.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client identifies the draft’s decision: “the title and description have to be typed in by hand” and automatic title retrieval “is left out”; the client supplies the correction: “the app fetches the page's title automatically, and I can still edit it.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client rejects the manual-only title/description workflow and supplies the reference-conforming automatic retrieval behavior. This decision concerns the presented title/description portion of metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “bulk import/export are deferred from v1”; round 1 client explicitly responds, “I'm fine leaving out … import/export.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, Netscape-format import and export are omitted. The client explicitly identifies and accepts that departure, rather than merely giving bare approval.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Pasting a valid URL” starts metadata retrieval; round 4 maker explicitly describes the MVP as “paste a URL … save,” and the round 4 client approves “saving and reopening a link.”
decisions.note: The revised specification and task breakdown record saving a bookmark from a URL, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker characterizes the revision as “automatic metadata retrieval” but enumerates only page title and short description; favicon and preview image are not included. Round 2 client repeats only “the title fills in … with a description” and approves the specification.
decisions.note: The revised metadata decision remains narrower than REF-BM-02 because it omits automatic favicon and preview-image collection. The client does not state that difference or request alignment; approval alone does not demonstrate awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: title and description are automatically filled and “Both fields remain editable”; round 2 client confirms, “I can still edit both.”
decisions.note: The revised specification permits editing the collected title and description, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker describes US1 as saving and being able to “reopen it”; round 4 client understands and approves this as “saving and reopening a link.”
decisions.note: At task review, revisiting the saved original link is recorded in functionally equivalent language.
